note: MEASURED gap inventory between get_errors (the reference) and get_incidents (the successor).
Produced by internal/tools/get_errors_oracle_test.go, which drives both tools' real filter
builders and real projections over one shared seeded state and reflects over both schemas.
This file is a RATCHET, not a snapshot. It fails in both directions:
- a gap closes -> shrink this file in the SAME commit that closes it;
- a new divergence appears -> that is a regression, fix the code, not this file.
Regenerate with: AGNT_ORACLE_REGOLD=1 go test ./internal/tools/ -run DivergenceMatchesGolden
(the regen still fails the test on purpose, so a stale golden cannot be laundered green).
STATUSES:
to_be_closed          - an open divergence; whether it BLOCKS is decided by availability below.
permanently_justified - owner decision, never to be closed; rationale is inline.
get_errors_defect     - get_incidents is BETTER here; does not block the superset,
recorded so the migration does not port the defect forward.
AVAILABILITY (to_be_closed entries only) - the owner's bar is AVAILABILITY, not exactness:
the information get_errors surfaced must be REACHABLE through get_incidents. Identical ids,
counts, labels, ordering and dedup granularity are NOT required.
data_missing          - absent or destroyed upstream, unrecoverable by any caller. BLOCKS deletion.
presentation_differs  - reachable; only shape, name or accounting differs. Does NOT block.
get_errors can be deleted exactly when no data_missing entry remains - and even then only after
adapter coverage is confirmed, since this oracle measures projection and schema, not live output.
availability is a REVIEWED ARTIFACT, NOT A LEVER: demoting an entry to presentation_differs is the
one cheap way to open the gate without closing a gap, so the distribution is pinned in the test and
a demotion must change the measurement, this file, and those numbers together.
MECHANISM CITATION (required): a name probe measures SCHEMA PRESENCE; availability asks
REACHABILITY. Those are different questions, and any fact that migrated into free text, a blob, or a
composite field is scored missing by a name probe purely because nothing bears its name. Every
availability_reason must therefore name the mechanism it consulted - field name, summary text, blob
hydration, context struct, adapter inputs, or capability/signal absence. 'No field has this name' is
NOT sufficient evidence of unreachability; item.location is the worked example, where the name check
is refuted and the entry still blocks for measured reasons.

divergences.availability_reason: MECHANISM CONSULTED: the returned record set. The matched records themselves come back, so 'how many matched my filter' is countable client-side; only which count the tool chooses to report differs. No underlying fact is destroyed.
divergences.get_errors: error_count/warning_count = the returned, deduped, filtered set (counted before the display limit)
divergences.get_incidents: inbox_after = whole-inbox band occupancy after the query, independent of what this page returned
divergences.detail: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and genuinely closeable: this fires only while the two quantities actually disagree on the seed AND get_incidents exposes no matched-set count. With warnings excluded get_errors reports warning_count=0 while the inbox warning band still holds 1. They answer different questions — 'how many matched your filter' vs 'how full is the inbox' — so a migration that maps error_count onto inbox_after.error is wrong. Closing this means giving get_incidents a count of the matched set (e.g. matched_count), not reusing the band stats.

divergences.availability_reason: MECHANISM CONSULTED: cursor paging. get_incidents is a cursor-based pull, so the whole matching set stays reachable to a caller that pages for it; only where the truncation happens differs.
divergences.get_errors: always requests 100, then limits for display after dedup+sort
divergences.get_incidents: forwards the caller's limit and truncates server-side
divergences.detail: Consequence for counts, not just page size: get_errors' error_count/warning_count describe the WHOLE matching set because it counts before trimming, whereas a limited get_incidents page reports a truncated page plus whole-inbox band stats. A caller migrating a limited query gets different totals. See counts.semantics.

divergences.get_errors: forwards since verbatim (e.g. "5m"), which the hub cannot parse
divergences.get_incidents: resolves the duration to an absolute RFC3339 timestamp before querying
divergences.detail: Direction is REVERSED: get_incidents is correct, get_errors is not. Nothing is silently dropped — incidentQueryFilterToInternal (internal/daemon/hub_incidents.go) explicitly REJECTS an unparseable since rather than returning the whole inbox, and the handler maps that to ErrInvalidArgs, so no Silent Failure Prohibition violation ships today. The real defect is a PATH FORK: the rejected query makes collectIncidentErrors return ok=false, and get_errors falls through to its legacy collectors, which DO parse durations correctly. So `since:"5m"` is answered by a different code path than the same query without it — different ids (abcbbf1a vs fp-js), different source vocabulary (browser:js vs browser_js), and legacy frame-aware dedup instead of fingerprint dedup. Same input, two code paths, two answers. Does not block the superset; recorded so the migration does not port the fork forward, and so nobody 'fixes' get_incidents to match the reference here.
Deliberately excluded from the superset. get_errors keeps it; get_incidents must not gain it.
divergences.rationale: Owner decision: global was a debugging affordance, not a production use case. The incident inbox is per-session hard-isolated (numbered contract 1, .claude/rules/daemon-architecture.md) — a stronger guarantee than project scoping. Closing this gap would mean weakening that isolation, which is expressly forbidden. This entry is permanent and must NOT be removed when the others are.

divergences.availability_reason: MECHANISM CONSULTED: the CallToolResult content, not the typed struct. The same rendered text is returned there, so every caller receives it and only the transport differs — the definition of a presentation difference under the availability bar.
divergences.get_errors: summary: rendered text in the typed output struct
divergences.detail: Transport difference rather than lost information: get_incidents renders the same compact text into the CallToolResult content instead of a typed output field. Callers that read the struct (not the content) see nothing. Low severity, but it is a real shape change for the migration.

divergences.get_incidents: preserves critical as a distinct band
divergences.detail: Direction is REVERSED: get_incidents carries strictly more information. A get_errors caller cannot tell a critical from an ordinary error. Recorded so the migration does not re-flatten the scale to match the reference.

divergences.get_incidents: preserves info as a distinct band
divergences.detail: Direction is REVERSED: get_incidents carries strictly more information. A get_errors caller cannot tell a critical from an ordinary error. Recorded so the migration does not re-flatten the scale to match the reference.

divergences.availability_reason: MECHANISM CONSULTED: label mapping between the two vocabularies. Every legacy label has an enum counterpart naming the same source, so the origin of an error is fully reachable and only the spelling differs — a migration cost for saved filters and docs, not lost information.
divergences.get_errors: colon-delimited: browser:js process: proxy:diagnostic proxy:http startup
divergences.get_incidents: underscore enum: browser_js http_5xx http_4xx proxy_diag process_alert build_fail …
divergences.detail: UNPREDICTED. get_errors itself speaks two vocabularies: its legacy collectors emit browser:js / proxy:http / proxy:diagnostic / process:<id>, while its incident shim passes the pipeline's enum through verbatim. So the same tool labels the same error differently depending on which path served it. Any caller (or doc, or saved filter) keyed on the legacy strings breaks on migration, and get_incidents' sources[] filter accepts only the enum form.
